title: mine evidence to extend US_STATES for US
headline: US_STATES needs no extension (47/52 keys evidenced; only 'del' 10711 and 'penn' 3084 are LIKELY additions). NEW: the US corpus has two incompatible state dialects - sources 1-2 write 2-letter codes, source 3 writes full names (code/name ratio 35-37 vs 0.10) - and ADDR_CANON_COMMON leaves 396959 ordinal occurrences (77.67%) un-normalised.

key_number.unit: uncanonicalised ordinal occurrences in US addr_tokens across all 6 profiles

new_defects.name: US state dialect split by source
new_defects.detail: sources 1 and 2 write the 2-letter state code, source 3 writes the full state name; no file is intermediate
new_defects.artefact_warning: The apparent aggregate code/name ratio of ~1.44 (25 states in [1.30,1.60], median 1.4404) is a mixing artefact of name-dominant and code-dominant files, not a per-state property. Per-file the same states swing 0.041 to 202.7 (texas 186.9 in tr_s1 vs 0.052 in tr_s3).

new_defects.name: ADDR_CANON_COMMON ordinal canonicalisation stops at fifth
new_defects.detail: normalize.py:184 maps only first->1st .. fifth->5th. 'First Ave' and '1st Ave' unify but 'Sixth Ave' and '6th Ave' do not ('sixth' vs '6th').

us_states_audit.notable: michigan 7822 and nevada 3472 occur as names while mi and nv are 0 - written out in full, never abbreviated

candidates.note: classic Del. abbreviation; not in US_STATES

leet_audit.unreachable_reason: _non_alnum=[^a-z0-9]+ (normalize.py:269) splits on them before t.translate(LEET) at line 280, so no surviving token can contain @ or $
leet_audit.only_unmapped_digit_token: 24hr (3657) - a legitimate abbreviation, not leetspeak, so the missing 2->z mapping has no measured cost

gaps: Multi-word US_STATES keys are unmeasurable: TOKEN_RE=[a-z0-9]+ and ADDR_SPLIT=[,;] store 'New York' as separate tokens new(519714) and york(384608); no bigram/component field exists. 14 keys unauditable.
Suspected D.C. defect unquantified: normalize.py:331 turns 'D.C.' into 'd c' with a space while smap holds 'dc'; profile has dc=35681 but cannot distinguish dotted from undotted.
Truncation: top-4000 per file, rank-4000 counts 201/407/440/101/258/274; absent from all six means <101 occurrences per file, not literally zero.
Hapax pruning (build_profile.py:45) deletes count==1 tokens every 8 chunks.
No row-level co-occurrence field, so 'del'/'penn' cannot be confirmed as standalone address components.
recommendations: P1 Extend ADDR_CANON_COMMON ordinals 5->20 (sixth..twentieth). Closes 77.67% of the ordinal gap, ~33 defects per 1000 US rows, low false-merge risk.
P2 Add 'del':'de' and 'penn':'pa' to US_STATES (LIKELY). 13795 additional components normalised. Do not add the 17 zero-count abbreviations.
P3 No change to US_STATES for territory/region names; no change to LEET.
P4 Investigate the F2 dialect split outside the dictionary - a state-string feature may be fitted on one dialect and scored on another.
P5 Add a component-level field to build_profile.py to close the multi-word key, D.C. and co-occurrence gaps.
